clue.text: Check metal used in sword

explanation.surface: Someone inspects the steel that goes into a blade.
explanation.walkthrough: A triple definition: the word means to thwart, a thin metal sheet, and a light fencing sword; 'used in' just joins the last two.
explanation.definitionFit: To thwart a plan is to check it; kitchen sheet metal and the blunt fencing weapon share the same name.

clue.text: With good intentions, keep providing protection for ancient city

indicators.note: a fort protecting something surrounds it, so the city goes inside

parts.note: a keep is a castle's stronghold, here a fort
Thebes was a great city of ancient Egypt and Greece

explanation.surface: A fortress keeps guarding an old city out of kindness.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom: doing something meaning well, even if it turns out badly, is done with that aim.

clue.text: Abuse of heroin's taking place near coast

indicators.note: abuse is misuse or mistreatment, so the letters of the following word are knocked about

explanation.surface: Drug misuse is happening by the seaside.
explanation.walkthrough: The possessive 's is counted here: the letters of HEROINS are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Inshore fishing or currents are those found close to the shore rather than out at sea.

clue.text: Go out with girl beside river

indicators.note: beside means the river is placed next to the girl

parts.note: Sally is a girl's name
the Forth is a Scottish river

explanation.surface: Someone takes a walk with a young woman along the riverbank.
explanation.definitionFit: To sally forth is an idiom for setting out boldly from a place.

clue.text: Strength's about to diminish without limit

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one word goes round the other

parts.note: to allay pain or fear is to lessen it
thew is an old word for muscular strength

explanation.surface: Someone's power is on the point of fading away completely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strength's about to diminish' reads as power waning, but the strength word sits with 'about' showing ALLAY going round it.
explanation.definitionFit: Going the whole distance without stopping is doing something to the full, with no limit.

clue.text: Identification left on murder victim

parts.note: Abel was killed by his brother Cain in Genesis, the first murder victim

explanation.surface: A name tag was found on the body of someone who was killed.
explanation.definitionFit: A tag that names or identifies something is attached to it to show what it is.

clue.text: Irregular bursts of activity suit French writer's floosies

parts.note: to suit is to fit, as clothes do
George Sand was a French novelist; possessive gives an S
floosies are loose women, tarts

explanation.surface: A French novelist's mistresses are presented as unpredictable outbursts.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for work done spasmodically, starting and stopping rather than steadily.

clue.text: The rest have to live without you in the end

indicators.note: without in its old sense means outside, so the verb goes round

parts.note: to reside is to live in a place

indicators.note: in the end points to the final letter of the word you

explanation.surface: Those remaining must carry on living once you are gone.
explanation.definitionFit: A residue is what is left over, the remainder after the rest is taken away.

clue.text: Note the Editor has' received

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held 'Note the Editor has' received' looks garbled (stray apostrophe); no parse gives HEED with each word doing one job: E for note inside HE'D needs 'Note' also to define.

clue.text: Fluster stirring calm

indicators.note: stirring mixes things up, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A bit of agitation proves soothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Restful and calm are synonyms for something peaceful and untroubled.

clue.text: Monopoly started here, with no preliminaries

explanation.surface: The board game began at a certain spot, straight away.
explanation.walkthrough: Monopoly players begin on the square marked GO, so the phrase read literally names where play starts.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for right from the very beginning, with nothing before; also literally the Monopoly starting square.

clue.text: Live without painter who's not right stuff

indicators.note: without means outside, so the verb goes round

parts.note: to live is to be, exist

indicators.note: not shows a letter being dropped from the painter

parts.note: a painter is an artist

explanation.surface: Life without an artist who isn't right is presented as material.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stuff' looks like a verb or general clutter, but here it means cloth; 'without' in its old sense means outside, and 'not right' drops the R for right.
explanation.definitionFit: Stuff means woven material, and batiste is a fine light cotton or linen fabric.

clue.text: Harbour Dutch pirate?

explanation.surface: A seaport is linked with a buccaneer from the Netherlands.
explanation.walkthrough: The port near Rotterdam doubles as a whimsical name for Captain Hook if he came from Holland.
explanation.definitionFit: A Dutch port and ferry terminal; read whimsically, a pirate named Hook who hails from Holland.

clue.text: Can cyanide (not iodine) mixed with sulphur produce the dominating influence?

indicators.note: mixed means stirred together, so the letters are rearranged
not shows a letter being dropped from the poison

parts.note: I is the chemical symbol for iodine
S is the chemical symbol for sulphur

explanation.surface: A chemistry question asks whether a cyanide mix with sulphur could take control.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove I from CYANIDE to get CYANDE, then rearrange CAN + CYANDE + S.
explanation.definitionFit: Ascendancy is the state of having dominant power or controlling influence over others.

clue.text: Sound sheepish after table gets broken

indicators.note: something broken is in pieces, so the letters are reassembled

explanation.surface: Someone sounds embarrassed after a piece of furniture is smashed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sound sheepish' reads as feeling ashamed, but means make the noise a sheep makes.
explanation.definitionFit: To make the cry of a sheep is literally to sound like one.

clue.text: Peculiarity dam has, in turn, to transmit to son.

parts.note: a weir is a low dam across a river

indicators.note: in turn signals turning the transmit word around

parts.note: to send is to transmit

explanation.surface: An odd tale of a mother passing something down to her boy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dam' looks like a mother animal but is a river barrier; SEND reversed gives DNES.
explanation.definitionFit: Weirdness is the quality of being strange or odd, a peculiarity.

clue.text: I had energy to go up and hit Henry -—- that's in character

parts.note: I'd is the short form of I had
E is the physics symbol for energy

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the word is read upwards, backwards

parts.note: taken as written
to rap is to strike
H is the symbol for the henry, the unit of inductance

explanation.surface: Someone full of energy rises and strikes a man named Henry, which is typical of them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that's in character' sounds like 'typical', but 'character' is a written symbol.
explanation.definitionFit: An ideograph is a written character standing for an idea, as in Chinese script.

clue.text: Fat that could replace flat

explanation.surface: Something flabby could stand in for a deflated thing.
explanation.walkthrough: A roll of fat round the waist and the extra wheel kept for a puncture share a name.
explanation.definitionFit: The slang for a roll of flab at the waist; also the reserve wheel used after a puncture.

clue.text: Hoped diapers were disposable

indicators.note: disposable suggests being thrown away and redone, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone wished the nappies were the throwaway kind.
explanation.definitionFit: To aspire is to hope or aim for something, so aspired matches hoped.

clue.text: It could be the perfect figure, but she's heartless

parts.note: ten is a number, a figure

indicators.note: heartless removes the middle, leaving the first and last letters of she

explanation.surface: She would be the ideal shape, but she is cruel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the perfect' looks like an ideal, but it is the perfect tense in grammar.
explanation.definitionFit: The perfect is a grammatical tense, so it is one example of the class.

clue.text: Gear in a nondescript colour

explanation.surface: Clothing in a dull shade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gear' suggests clothing but means the car gear where none is engaged.
explanation.definitionFit: The out-of-gear position in a car; also a dull beige or grey shade.

clue.text: Establishment — 24 things are tested here

parts.note: proving something is establishing it
the answer to 24 means worn down, which is ground

explanation.surface: A place where items are put through trials.
explanation.definitionFit: A proving ground is a site where weapons, vehicles or ideas are tested.

clue.text: Home help turns up in the country

parts.note: in means at home

indicators.note: in a down clue turns up means the word is read upwards

parts.note: aid is help

explanation.surface: A domestic helper arrives in a nation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Home help' reads as a domestic worker but splits into two pieces; 'turns up' reverses the help word because this is a down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: India is a country in South Asia.

clue.text: Bathe in state, briefly

indicators.note: briefly means cut short, so the state name is truncated

parts.note: Washington is a US state

explanation.surface: Someone bathes in a nervous state for a moment.
explanation.definitionFit: To wash and to bathe both mean to clean with water.

clue.text: Jack's surprisingly set upon'disposing of one that's worn down

parts.note: a jack or jack tar is a sailor, AB for able seaman

indicators.note: disposing of means getting rid of a letter

parts.note: raided means attacked by surprise
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A sailor is ambushed, getting rid of a tired old thing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jack' is a sailor, not a name or a lifting tool; 'disposing of' removes the I for one from the attack word.
explanation.definitionFit: Abraded means scraped or eroded away by friction.

clue.text: A group of players took part in race —- one that didn't win

parts.note: LSO is the London Symphony Orchestra
ran means competed in a race

explanation.surface: An orchestra entered a race and lost.
explanation.walkthrough: 'group of players' suggests a team, but it is the orchestra.
explanation.definitionFit: An also-ran is a contestant who finished unplaced, a loser.

clue.text: Extremely hungry a couple of times, drinking tiny amount of liquid at water cure

indicators.note: drinking means taking in, so the drop goes inside
a couple of times means the picked letters are used twice
extremely points to the outer letters, first and last, of hungry

parts.note: a drop is a tiny quantity of liquid

explanation.surface: A starving person sipping a little water at a health spa.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a couple of times' doubles the outer letters of hungry, and 'drinking' puts the drop and 'at' between the two copies.
explanation.definitionFit: Hydropathy is the treatment of disease by water, a spa therapy.

clue.text: Scope, moving to oppose or cooperate

explanation.surface: Range, motion, rivalry or teamwork.
explanation.walkthrough: A triple definition: room to move, a move in a game, and to compete against or go along with.
explanation.definitionFit: Free movement or room is play; a move in a game is a play; to play is to compete or to cooperate.
